clue.text: Study anything but arts. That's good sense!

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
the sciences are the academic field set against the arts

explanation.surface: A student boasts that avoiding the humanities is simply the sensible choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscience is the inner moral sense of right and wrong, a kind of good judgement.

clue.text: Order the thing or forget?

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
it stands for the thing

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to command something or let it slip from mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit is to leave out or neglect, as when one fails to remember.

clue.text: The boy attending a musical presentation

parts.note: a son is a male child
to be at an event is to attend it

explanation.surface: A lad goes along to a concert or show.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a classical composition for one or two instruments, performed as a piece.

clue.text: An American soldier set up superior base

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a GI is a US soldier
noble means grand or of high rank

explanation.surface: A US serviceman establishes a top-class military camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a military camp; it means low or contemptible.
explanation.definitionFit: Base and ignoble both mean dishonourable or mean in character.

clue.text: Mark's sound

definitions.meaning: a written sign or annotation, a jotted reminder

explanation.definitionFit: A note is a written mark or memo, and also a musical tone heard.

clue.text: Spectator having look round

parts.note: to eye is to look at
a ball is round, a sphere

explanation.surface: Someone watching takes a glance about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look' wants to be the definition, but the wordplay ends the clue; the whole organ is playfully cast as the one watching.
explanation.definitionFit: The eyeball is the organ that does the watching, so whimsically it is the spectator.

clue.text: Popular with evil Arab agitators just the same

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: agitators stir things up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Wicked rabble-rousers enjoy steady public support.
explanation.definitionFit: Invariable means never changing, always staying constant.

clue.text: Posted a note in payment for accommodation, giving offence

indicators.note: in says the two pieces go inside the payment

parts.note: rent is paid for lodging
sent means mailed or posted
me is a variant spelling of mi, the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone mailed a message with their rent, and it caused upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offence' is the feeling of having been offended, as in 'take offence'.
explanation.definitionFit: Resentment is bitter indignation, the feeling of taking umbrage.

clue.text: No longer a part of special occasion celebrations

indicators.note: a part of says the letters sit as a run inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something that used to feature in festivities for a big day has stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'occasion' and the start of 'celebrations'.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some past time but not now.

clue.text: Men get into trouble for making a bloomer

indicators.note: to get into trouble is to be thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Men land themselves in a scrape by committing a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bloomer' looks like a blunder; it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mignonette is a fragrant garden flower, and a bloomer is anything that flowers.

clue.text: Causing conflict in a worker's mind

indicators.note: in says the war is placed within the insect

parts.note: a worker bee is the classic crossword worker
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: An employee is privately stirring up strife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mind' looks like a noun; it is the verb, as in 'mind the step'.
explanation.definitionFit: To beware is to take heed or be careful of something, just as 'mind' does as a command.

clue.text: Mean with 18-or so the story goes

parts.note: par is the average or normal level, a mean
the answer to 18 across, meaning clever

explanation.surface: A tale is told of someone average yet capable.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a short moral tale told to teach a lesson.

clue.text: He often takes a dip-but never wants porridge afterwards

definitions.text: He often takes a dip-but never wants porridge afterwards

parts.words: He often takes a dip-but never wants porridge afterwards
parts.note: a dip is slang for stealing from pockets, and porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, which this thief hopes to avoid

explanation.surface: A swimmer who never fancies oatmeal after a plunge.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is British slang for time served in prison; dipping is slang for stealing from pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who steals from people's pockets in crowds is said to dip.

clue.text: On the square? That makes the lag grin!

indicators.note: makes means the letters are made into something else

explanation.surface: A convict grins at being told that he is now honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the square' looks like 'honest'; it means at ninety degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: A set square gives ninety degrees, so 'on the square' means at a perpendicular corner.

clue.text: Person dining in the latest brasserie, a terrific place

indicators.note: in signals the letters run inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone having a meal at the newest bistro, a wonderful venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts with the last letter of 'brasserie' and ends inside 'terrific'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eater is one who consumes food, someone having a meal.

clue.text: Lost fir somehow, but she has flowers

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some new way

explanation.surface: A tree has gone missing from the plot, though a woman still has blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A florist is a shopkeeper who sells cut blooms and bouquets.

clue.text: The fellow always in turmoil

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'for ever'

explanation.surface: A man who is perpetually in a state of agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Fever means feverish excitement or agitation, as in a fever of anticipation.

clue.text: Moderate on the Left offering support

parts.note: to ease is to lessen or moderate

explanation.surface: A centrist on the political left offers backing.
explanation.walkthrough: Political 'moderate' and 'Left' are a false scene; the words just give EASE and L.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that holds up a painting or blackboard.

clue.text: Silver taken in church, just a pound

indicators.note: taken in means the metal is placed inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Coins collected at a church service came to only a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money; it is an enclosure for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A pound is an enclosure for stray animals, so a kind of pen or coop.

clue.text: A blockhead the French find clever

parts.note: the head of the word block is its first letter, B
le is the masculine French word for the

explanation.surface: French people decide a dunce is actually bright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blockhead' looks like a fool; read as 'block head' it is the first letter of block.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means skilled or competent, a near synonym of clever.

clue.text: Both men and women can be regressive

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, and this word reads identically that way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: People of either gender are capable of going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Men and women are the two genders, the male and female of the species.

clue.text: A politician finds his constituents aren't so bad

indicators.note: bad means faulty, so the letters are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawmaker discovers that his voters are not really so awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' hints at the letters forming the answer, but it is part of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, an elected legislator.

clue.text: Do whatever is needed to maintain such a tree

definitions.text: Do whatever is needed to maintain
definitions.meaning: to keep a car or machine in working order
the sorb or wild ... tree, a European tree of the rose family

explanation.definitionFit: To service a machine is to maintain it, and the service tree is a European tree related to rowan.

clue.text: Fresh perch. It is cooked in a jug

indicators.note: fresh suggests a new form of the letters
cooked means prepared or tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newly caught fish is cooked in an earthenware vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitcher is a large jug with a lip for pouring.

clue.text: Split-about time! — for use in a laboratory

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a rent is a split or tear
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A divided group asks for some time before going to work in a lab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tells you to wrap the split round the time; the split's middle opens after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a chemical substance used in laboratory tests and reactions.

clue.text: A vehicle for the young to move about with facility

parts.note: to go is to move
c is short for circa, Latin for about
art means skill or facility

explanation.surface: Children's transport can be driven around with ease.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-cart is a small toy cart children ride or push.

clue.text: Can't or possibly can appear on the other side

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be ordered another way

explanation.surface: Whether one can or cannot, it may be necessary to appear for the opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Contra is Latin for against, used to mean taking the opposing position.

clue.text: Count in German

parts.note: the German noble title equal to an earl or count, not a numeral

explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' could mean counting numbers in German; it is the noble title.
explanation.definitionFit: A German nobleman of this rank is equivalent to a count or earl.

clue.text: The brotherhood-many imprisoned

annotationWithheld.why: The brotherhood-many imprisoned (4): L (many, fifty) inside CAN, but 'imprisoned' must give CAN and also be the container indicator

clue.text: May be finished, so call in 18

parts.note: to term something is to call or name it
taken as written
the answer to 18 across, meaning clever

explanation.surface: Something may be completed, so summon a capable person.
explanation.definitionFit: Something terminable can be brought to an end or concluded.

clue.text: A woman bearing with each and every reverse

parts.note: E is short for each

indicators.note: reverse means the word for every is read backwards

parts.note: all means every one

explanation.surface: A lady is putting up with every setback.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a female given name, so it names a particular woman.

clue.text: Contemplating bouncing back?

definitions.meaning: thinking deeply or musing over something
throwing light or sound back from a surface, as a mirror does

explanation.definitionFit: Reflecting means pondering, and also sending light or an image back like a mirror.
